items.title: FPL LIVE RANK! What You Need To Know 📊
items.headline: FPL.page and FPL Focal launch live rank tool using official FPL data
items.summary:
FPL managers can now track their live overall rank through FPL.page and the FPL Focal app, with the tool pulling directly from the official Fantasy Premier League feed for full rank accuracy.

The live rank feature factors in key in-game updates including live bonus points, auto substitutions and defensive contribution points, giving managers a more complete picture of their gameweek position before the official update.

To use it, managers only need their FPL ID. This can be found on the FPL website by opening the Points page and copying the number shown in the page URL. Entering that ID at FPL.page/rank or in the FPL Focal app returns the live rank instantly.

items.headline: Bruno Fernandes takes Gameweek 1 armband as Szoboszlai shapes an early Bench Boost squad
items.summary:
The Gameweek 1 squad locks in with the Bench Boost active and Bruno Fernandes captained for Manchester United’s trip to Hull. Erling Haaland stays in the team despite not taking the armband in either of the first two gameweeks, because he is likely to be needed as captain in Gameweeks 3 and 5 and selling him would force awkward transfers or an early chip. Bruno gets the nod because Hull and Ipswich in the opening two fixtures make him feel the safest captaincy route, even if Haaland’s ownership and Gameweek 1 record remain a clear risk.

Dominik Szoboszlai is the key late structural call. He comes into midfield alongside Bryan Mbeumo, Bruno and Solace, with the appeal built on Liverpool’s strong opening five fixtures and Szoboszlai’s security for 90-minute starts. Wirtz is viewed as having more upside, but Szoboszlai is preferred as the safer longer-term Liverpool route. The compromise is a lighter defence and a cheaper eighth attacker, with Brighton’s Gomez taking the final midfield slot despite being identified as the weakest pick.

The Bench Boost is built around Kinsky, Calafiori, Maguire, Rodon, Ajer, Dop, Verbruggen and Gomez, with the front line of Haaland, Dominic Calvert-Lewin and João Pedro unchanged throughout pre-season. Verbruggen, Ajer, Dop and Gomez are the boost players, all expected to start and all with playable home fixtures or Defcon routes. The target is modest: a double-digit Bench Boost is acceptable, with one clean sheet, one attacking return or a couple of Defcon scores likely enough to make the chip worthwhile.

There is heavy awareness of the trade-offs. Rodon is selected over Muharemovic because the money is needed elsewhere, even though Muharemovic has the better Defcon profile. Maguire is preferred to Shaw for greater set-piece threat and some Defcon potential, especially with Casemiro absent. Ajer is treated as a 5.0-style Defcon defender at 4.5, while Gomez is kept over Slater or Nottingham Forest’s Sangare because he has more attacking upside and useful Gameweek 3-4 fixtures against Leeds and Coventry. The plan is to roll transfers early, possibly move Mbeumo around Gameweeks 3-4, and Wildcard around Gameweek 6 unless the team can be stretched longer.
key_points: Bench Boost is active in Gameweek 1, with Wildcard 6 the current plan and no transfer planned for Gameweek 2.
Bruno Fernandes is captain over Haaland for Hull away; Haaland stays because he is wanted for captaincy in Gameweeks 3 and 5.
Dominik Szoboszlai is preferred to Wirtz for Liverpool coverage because of minutes security and strong opening fixtures.
Final squad structure is light in defence: Kinsky, Calafiori, Maguire and Rodon start, with Verbruggen, Ajer, Dop and Gomez forming the Bench Boost bench.
Gomez is the main uncertain spot, but he is kept over Slater or Sangare because Brighton’s injuries and fixtures give him short-term upside.

items.headline: Bruno Fernandes gets the armband as Haaland is sold for an aggressive Gameweek 1 bench boost
items.summary:
The Gameweek 1 plan lands on the aggressive side: Bench Boost is active immediately, Bruno Fernandes is captain, and Erling Haaland is left out despite Manchester City hosting Bournemouth. The logic is that if Haaland is not being captained, his £14m-plus price can be spread across a stronger 15-man squad for the opening bench boost. It is a high-risk call because Haaland is expected to start and score, but the bet is that Bruno, plus the upgraded players around the squad, can match or beat him over the opening weeks.

The final structure is a no-Haaland bench-boost squad built around David Raya in goal, Arsenal defensive cover through Riccardo Calafiori rather than Gabriel, Harry Maguire, Ballard, Nico Williams and the short-term De Cuyper punt. In midfield, Bruno Fernandes is locked as captain, with attacking upside also coming from Antoine Semenyo and Zolis after a late switch away from a safer Ben White/Ndiaye combination. Alexander Isak and Joao Pedro are key forward picks, with Isak effectively asked to cover the Haaland omission before a likely reset.

The whole approach points strongly towards an early Wildcard, most likely in Gameweek 3. That allows an immediate move back to Haaland for Manchester City’s fixture swing, alongside possible City additions such as Nico O’Reilly or Phil Foden if minutes look secure. The alternative Haaland draft is acknowledged as safer and more “classic FPL”, with a cheaper bench of players such as Gomez and O’Shea, but it offers less upside for Bench Boost and still probably leads to an early Wildcard because of Chelsea, Arsenal and City fixture swings.

The main risks are obvious: Arsenal could lose the clean sheet, Bruno could blank as captain, and Haaland could punish the fade with a brace or hat-trick against Bournemouth. There are also minutes doubts around Calafiori, De Cuyper and some of the mid-price punts. But the call is deliberately made now: attack Gameweek 1 with 15 players, roll in Gameweek 2 if possible, then Wildcard in Gameweek 3 to rebuild around Haaland, City and Chelsea information.
key_points: Bench Boost is active in Gameweek 1 to exploit a strong 15-man squad and avoid saving the chip for uncertain future doubles.
Bruno Fernandes is captain ahead of Haaland, with penalties and security making him the preferred armband despite Haaland’s Bournemouth fixture.
Erling Haaland is omitted in the final draft; the plan is to bring him back on a Gameweek 3 Wildcard unless circumstances change.
David Raya is retained as the Arsenal defensive anchor, with Calafiori selected but Gabriel ultimately missed in the final no-Haaland structure.
Late move: Zolis and Nico Williams come in over the safer Ben White/Ndiaye combination, increasing upside but adding regret risk.
Semenyo is valued for the early fixture run and especially Gameweek 3, while Isak is trusted as the premium forward placeholder before the Wildcard.
De Cuyper is treated as a short-term Bench Boost punt who needs an early Wildcard to manage minutes and fixture risk.
Gameweek 3 Wildcard targets include Haaland, possible Manchester City assets such as O’Reilly or Foden, and Chelsea players from Gameweek 4.

items.headline: Haaland fear versus triple Arsenal defence shapes the final Gameweek 1 call
items.summary:
Brighton's European lineup is the main late team-news warning. The side is close to full strength, with Pascal Groß playing another 90 minutes but still expected to start Aston Villa at home because Brighton are short of options and he keeps set pieces and possible penalties. Diego Gómez is back and looks the standout 5.0 midfielder despite likely early substitutions, while De Cuyper is a tempting short-term 4.5 defensive punt if he starts on the left wing. Veltman is less secure because Dunk could return, so Caicedo is the safer Brentford defensive route for those wanting nailed minutes rather than upside.

Elsewhere, Arsenal minutes are the major concern. Bukayo Saka and Declan Rice are fit enough to be involved against Coventry, but neither looks trustworthy enough for FPL from the start, especially with tougher fixtures to follow. Ben White looks safe for the first three to four weeks while Timber is not training with the group. At Chelsea, the penalty-taker noise is noted but Cole Palmer is still expected to keep them, while João Pedro remains the clear No 9. For Manchester United, De Ligt missing out strengthens Harry Maguire's short-term appeal, while Sesko returning to training creates a longer-term minutes worry for Bryan Mbeumo if he is pushed away from the striker role.

The preferred value calls are pragmatic rather than flashy. Ndiaye is the favourite 6.0 midfielder because he is nailed and on penalties, with Semenyo and Enzo Le Fee strong alternatives depending on structure and time horizon. Enzo Le Fee is more of a three-game punt before Sunderland's fixtures and European workload become a concern. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is the preferred 6.0 forward thanks to minutes and penalties, ahead of Brobbey, Igor Jesus and Gonzalo García. In defence, Harry Maguire is favoured at 5.0, Luke Shaw is a viable 4.5 saving, Ajer is one of the best 4.5 Def Con options, and Dan Ballard is an aggressive early wildcard pick because of set-piece threat and defensive contribution potential.

The current Gameweek 1 draft is a balanced Haaland team: Bragan in goal; Calafiori, Neco Williams and Maguire in defence; Bruno Fernandes, Benrahma, Szoboszlai and Groß in midfield; and Haaland, João Pedro and Calvert-Lewin up front, with Kinski, Gómez, O'Shea and Ballard on the bench. It is safe and flexible, but it only carries one Arsenal player, one Manchester City player and one Chelsea player into early fixture swings. The aggressive alternative drops Haaland for Isak, plays a triple Arsenal defence of Raya, Ben White and Calafiori, adds Mbeumo, Semenyo and Ndiaye, and plans to wildcard in Gameweek 3. Haaland at home to Bournemouth is still scary, but Bruno Fernandes against Hull is a live captaincy rival, especially if Haaland's minutes are capped after a light preseason.

{"headline":"Bruno Fernandes looks essential early as Solis becomes the Gameweek 1 gamble","summary":"Gameweek 1 plans centre on short-term fixture attacks rather than building a squad to last months. Bruno Fernandes is treated as close to essential for Manchester United’s opening two matches, starting away at Hull and followed by another promoted side, because he still offers penalties, set pieces, defensive contribution routes and proven FPL output. He is not necessarily a season-long hold at £12.0m, but the early fixtures are strong enough to justify starting with him and reassessing around Gameweek 3, when Liverpool, Manchester City and Chelsea assets become easier to target.

The most divisive pick is Arsenal’s new left-sided attacker Solis for Coventry at home in Gameweek 1. The upside is obvious: he looks sharp in the Community Shield, Martinelli appears out of favour, and Arsenal’s Friday-night opener is the kind of fixture that can trigger a huge ownership and price swing if he hauls. The risks are just as clear: he may rarely play 90 minutes, he is new to this Arsenal role, the fixtures quickly stiffen after Coventry, and a blank could make him an immediate sell. He is a viable two-to-three-week punt, but not a safe long-term selection.

Liverpool’s midfield also drives much of the debate. Florian Wirtz has the more exciting advanced role near Alexander Isak, but there is concern that his pre-season has shown clever link play rather than enough end product. Dominik Szoboszlai is the more pragmatic pick: £0.5m cheaper, likely to play 90 minutes, involved in set pieces, capable of defensive contributions from the double pivot and potentially moving into the No 10 role when Wirtz is withdrawn. For managers choosing between Wirtz and Morgan Rogers, the answer depends on structure: Liverpool’s Newcastle and Nottingham Forest fixtures make Wirtz attractive early, while Chelsea’s better run from Gameweek 4 makes Rogers a strong later target.

Premium decisions remain uncomfortable. Cole Palmer still carries doubts after an uneven pre-season and a niggle, while Isak has upside as Liverpool’s main striker with Ekitike out but also has ongoing fitness and minutes concerns.
